groups.title: Particle structure and identity
groups.proposal: Use Lesson 3 as the canonical particle source model while keeping conjectural origins and missing evidence non-authorizing.
groups.writingJob: Keep a particle monomorphemic and preserve its typed identity, attachment, spelling, and exceptional structure.
groups.readingJob: Help the reader recognize particles, attachment marks, stress, and uncertain historical analyses.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies or selects the intended particle; the application validates its structure and attachment.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the open particle source and existing particle choice. Do not expose syllable count, historical origin, or attachment mechanics as controls.

groups.title: Particle use and structural limits
groups.proposal: Make particle rank and function affect normal application behavior, not merely a label or explanation.
groups.writingJob: Allow particles in their licensed functions and block them from unlicensed matrix, principal-clause, or compound roles.
groups.readingJob: Guide recognition of adverbial, exclamatory, independent, and embedded particle uses.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended construction; the application decides whether the chosen particle can fill that structural role.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse construction and particle choices. Add no separate control for a restriction the application can check.

groups.title: Clause-introducing particles
groups.proposal: Treat clause introducers as genuine grammatical choices whose placement and compatibility are application duties.
groups.writingJob: Offer the licensed clause introducers and place each before the clause with its own force and applicability.
groups.readingJob: Guide the interpretation of ca, cuix, tlā, mā, and ō without replacing Nahuatl structure with an English label.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended clause force; the application limits the available particle choices and places the selected particle.
groups.controlPolicy: Use one contextual clause-introducer choice. Do not create separate controls for spelling, position, or English translation.

groups.title: The adjunctor in
groups.proposal: Unify optional adjunction with the existing clause relation system and keep translation non-authorizing.
groups.writingJob: Use optional in to mark an adjoined unit without treating it as a determiner.
groups.readingJob: Help the reader recover adjunction and resist English article-based analysis.
groups.decisionSplit: The user may choose optional explicit adjunction; the application keeps in out of a determiner slot and preserves the nuclear clause.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the clause-relation and particle paths. Never add a definite or indefinite article control for in.

groups.title: The conjunctor auh
groups.proposal: Keep one Nahuatl conjunction choice while allowing context-sensitive interpretation.
groups.writingJob: Offer auh for its licensed conjunction relation and place it between the related sentence units.
groups.readingJob: Guide the contextual reading of auh as and or but.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended relation; the application supplies licensed placement and Result structure.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the clause-relation choice; do not make English and versus but a second grammatical control unless Canvas requires a distinct Nahuatl choice.

groups.title: Adverbial particles
groups.proposal: Make lexical choice user-facing only where meaning is genuinely intended; keep realization automatic.
groups.writingJob: Offer adverbial particles with their licensed meanings, attachment, tense restrictions, and placement.
groups.readingJob: Guide contextual meanings and distinguish bound particles from similar-looking independent forms.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended meaning or discourse contribution; the application enforces attachment, tense, and placement.
groups.controlPolicy: Use a contextual particle choice. Derived attachment and tense compatibility stay automatic.

groups.title: Interjections and the vocative particle
groups.proposal: Separate genuine expressive choice from automatic vocative realization.
groups.writingJob: Generate licensed interjections and the bound vocative particle with speaker, repetition, attachment, and stress requirements.
groups.readingJob: Guide emotional force, speaker restrictions, repetition, and direct address.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended interjection or direct address; the application enforces speaker restrictions, attachment, repetition limits, and accent.
groups.controlPolicy: Use a contextual interjection or vocative choice. Do not expose obligatory attachment or accent as controls.

groups.title: Negative particle prefixes
groups.proposal: Make negative-prefix selection an application duty governed by the sentence environment.
groups.writingJob: Select ah# or ca# by grammatical environment, attach it to the following particle, and preserve licensed lexicalized combinations.
groups.readingJob: Help the reader recover negation, attachment, complementary distribution, and resulting lexical meanings.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses negation and intended construction; the application chooses ah# versus ca# and performs the boundary changes.
groups.controlPolicy: Use one negation choice. Never ask the user to choose the predictable negative prefix or its automatic sound change.

groups.title: Particle collocations
groups.proposal: Treat Lesson 3 itself as the particle sequence pipeline rather than concatenating interface labels.
groups.writingJob: Build licensed multi-particle sequences in fixed order, preserve separate writing, and handle lexicalized meanings and stress-group behavior.
groups.readingJob: Help the reader recover the members, order, attachment, and contextual meaning of a collocation.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended combined meaning or construction; the application builds the licensed sequence and order.
groups.controlPolicy: Prefer one construction choice for a lexicalized collocation and reuse canonical particle choices for productive sequences. Never expose slot order as user work.

groups.title: Honorificized particles
groups.proposal: Route particle honorificization through the shared grammar operation instead of a special display-only form.

groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses honorific intent when socially meaningful; the application derives the licensed particle form.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the honorific choice only for particles that license it. Do not expose suffix selection or internal derivation as controls.
